title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy proposes creating a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats inside the President’s Executive Office to monitor and respond to risks from AI and other advanced technologies. It also outlines additional duties for the office, such as coordinating national AI strategy, advising on policy, and ensuring secure technology development.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 establishes standards and oversight to ensure that AI systems developed in the United States are safe, transparent, and aligned with public interests. It requires rigorous testing, accountability measures, and collaboration between government, academia, and industry to promote trustworthy AI technologies.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board to investigate cybersecurity breaches involving AI technologies and to oversee AI safety standards. It aims to enhance transparency, accountability, and public trust in AI systems by setting clear guidelines for developers and requiring reporting of security incidents.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 establishes guidelines for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks associated with AI systems. It also creates oversight mechanisms and enforcement tools to ensure that organizations implement robust security measures to protect against misuse and unintended harm.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a new task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to assess and strengthen the security of artificial intelligence systems across the United States. The act aims to coordinate efforts between government agencies and private industry to identify AI vulnerabilities, develop safeguards, and promote best practices for AI security.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution formally creates a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to monitor and guide the development and use of AI technologies. It designates the committee’s role in evaluating AI’s impacts, setting standards, and recommending policy actions.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is legislation that restricts the use of artificial intelligence in medical diagnosis and treatment, ensuring that only licensed human doctors can perform critical patient care decisions. The law aims to protect patients from potential errors and maintain accountability by limiting AI's role to supportive tools rather than primary decision-makers.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a framework for assessing potential risks associated with AI systems, requiring detailed evaluations before they can be deployed. The act aims to protect public safety, privacy, and accountability by mandating risk assessments, transparent reporting, and regulatory oversight for AI technologies.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed regulatory framework aimed at governing the development, deployment, and use of AI technologies, ensuring they are safe, transparent, and aligned with societal values. It establishes guidelines for risk assessment, accountability, and oversight to protect users and promote responsible innovation in AI.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act temporarily stops the building and use of data centers specifically for artificial intelligence. It is intended to give lawmakers time to study the environmental, energy, and privacy impacts of these centers before deciding whether to allow them to resume.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a law designed to curb the environmental damage caused by AI technology. It requires developers and users to reduce carbon emissions, lower energy use, and safeguard natural resources as part of responsible AI practices.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act aims to promote the development and deployment of AI technologies that directly benefit the American public by ensuring they are accessible, affordable, and aligned with national interests. The legislation includes provisions for increased funding for AI research, safeguards against bias and misuse, and measures to foster collaboration between government, industry, and academia to drive responsible AI innovation.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is designed to ensure that students from kindergarten through twelfth grade gain essential understanding of artificial intelligence, including how it works and its societal impacts. It likely establishes national standards, resources, and teacher training programs to embed AI concepts across the curriculum, preparing students and educators for an increasingly AI‑driven world.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 aims to set clear standards and guidelines for developing AI systems that are trustworthy and dependable. It focuses on ensuring safety, transparency, and accountability in AI research and deployment to protect public interests.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to set up a pilot program that uses AI to defend critical infrastructure from cyber threats. The program aims to test AI-based tools and strategies to improve national security and protect essential systems.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a proposed federal law aimed at improving AI education and preparedness in elementary and secondary schools. It seeks to develop AI curricula, train teachers, and give students access to AI tools while addressing privacy, equity, and safety concerns.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act establishes rules to ensure that artificial intelligence systems used in Veterans Affairs claim processing are transparent, fair, and accountable. It requires regular audits, clear documentation of decision‑making, and mechanisms for addressing errors or biases that could affect veterans’ claims.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 is a law that requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to openly disclose how it uses artificial intelligence in its services, including the types of AI tools and data involved. It also mandates that veterans and regulators can review the decision‑making processes of those AI systems to ensure fairness, accountability, and public trust.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act aims to boost the public’s understanding of AI. It proposes a coordinated effort by government agencies to educate citizens on AI’s benefits, risks, and ethical considerations.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: This Senate resolution stresses that religious freedom should be protected and respected in all contexts. It also calls for the use of authoritative texts and demands greater transparency in how artificial intelligence systems are designed and operated.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law that requires companies to clearly label AI-generated content so people can easily tell it apart from human-made content. It aims to prevent deceptive practices by mandating disclosure of AI usage, protecting consumers from being misled by automated information.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress detailing how artificial intelligence systems are used to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. It aims to increase transparency and oversight of AI’s role in national‑security intelligence operations.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 aims to strengthen the U.S. workforce’s ability to work with AI by updating educational curricula, expanding training opportunities, and fostering partnerships between industry, academia, and government. The bill intends to ensure that workers, especially those in emerging tech fields, have the skills and knowledge needed to thrive in an AI‑driven economy.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act seeks to boost the growth and influence of open‑source artificial intelligence by providing funding, resources, and support to developers and research teams. It aims to foster collaboration, transparency, and innovation across the AI community through shared standards and public‑private partnerships.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 aims to prevent companies from inflating the costs of AI services and from manipulating labor wages in the AI industry. It establishes regulations and penalties to ensure fair pricing and protect workers from exploitative wage practices.
